scoring_justification: T1/T2 infeasible: paper values are only curves; the main claim is trends (monotonicity, ordering) which can be verified structurally without hidden reference numbers.

outputs.description: Mechanical and electrical damage components as functions of void volume fraction f and aspect ratio S. Each row corresponds to one simulation case. For spherical void scan, S=1.0; for aspect ratio scan, f=0.0654.
Directly extracted effective piezoelectric coefficients e31, e33, e15 for the same (f,S) parameter grid as the damage CSV. Used to verify transversely isotropic damage hypothesis and trends.

output_contract.notes: Verification is structural (T3): monotonicity of D11_M, D33_M with f; decrease of D33_M with increasing S; near-constancy of D11_E, D33_E with S; decreasing trends in e31, e33, e15 with f. Additional loose tolerance (±30%) against digitized reference curves ensures approximate quantitative agreement.

steps.description: File exists and contains required columns.
For spherical voids (S=1), D11_M and D33_M increase monotonically with volume fraction f.
For fixed f=0.0654, D33_M decreases with increasing S, D11_M increases slowly, D11_E and D33_E remain nearly constant.
For spherical voids (S=1), D11_M ≈ D33_M (mechanical damage is isotropic).
File exists and contains required columns.
Effective piezoelectric coefficients e31, e33, e15 decrease (in magnitude) with increasing f for S=1.
Piezoelectric coefficients show consistent trends with S (e33 and e15 decreasing, e31 nearly constant).
